priorStories.headline: Hurricane Trudy threatens Mexico’s Pacific coast
priorStories.body:
Hurricane Trudy was affecting west-central Mexico’s Pacific coast as a Category 2 storm, with sustained winds of 100 mph.

A hurricane warning covered the coast from Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes. The U.S. National Hurricane Center warned of dangerous storm surge and damaging waves along with flooding and mudslides.

priorStories.headline: French protests draw 550,000, with 400 arrests
priorStories.body:
About 550,000 people joined 110 marches over living costs and school conditions, according to France’s interior minister. Organizers estimated attendance at 800,000.

Authorities reported roughly 400 arrests after clashes, fires and looting in several cities. An investigation was opened after a protester in Saint-Etienne lost a hand.

priorStories.headline: Romanian jets shoot down two attack drones
priorStories.body:
Romanian F-16s shot down two jet-powered Geran attack drones after they entered the country’s airspace over its territorial waters, Romania’s Defence Ministry said.

The drones were downed southeast and east of Sulina. The ministry said one spent two minutes in Romanian airspace and the other five minutes.

priorStories.headline: Kolkata festival crowd crush kills at least 19
priorStories.body:
At least 19 people died and 25 were injured in a crowd crush at a Durga Puja pavilion in north Kolkata, officials said.

The crush occurred Saturday night as people near the religious festival site sought shelter from rain.

candidates.summary: An overnight Ukrainian drone attack caused fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal, the Ruchi oil depot and other sites in and around St. Petersburg, Russian officials said. Governor Alexander Beglov reported one person killed and five wounded. Russia’s Defense Ministry said air defenses destroyed 1,015 drones across multiple regions, occupied Crimea and the Black Sea; the claims were not independently verified.
candidates.title: Drone attack ignites fires at St. Petersburg oil sites

candidates.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said Sunday that the number of arrests arising from Saturday’s nationwide protests had risen to 1,800. He also said more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters had been injured and that the casualty count remained provisional. The update substantially revised figures reported Saturday night.
candidates.title: France raises protest arrest count to 1,800

candidates.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection in Israel’s October 27 election. Netanyahu thanked Trump in a statement issued by his Likud party. The endorsement followed months in which Trump had declined to explicitly back Netanyahu’s campaign.
candidates.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu for reelection

candidates.summary: Pope Leo XIV appeared at the Apostolic Palace window for the traditional Sunday Angelus, four days after surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung because of a malignant tumor. He thanked those who prayed for him and said he would gradually resume his duties. The surgery confirmed adenocarcinoma.
candidates.title: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties

candidates.summary: French authorities said Sunday that at least 1,800 people had been arrested following Saturday’s nationwide protests. Hundreds of demonstrators gathered again at Paris’ Place de la République, where police used tear gas as tensions flared. President Emmanuel Macron scheduled an emergency meeting and an evening address. The Interior Ministry previously said more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured.
candidates.title: France raises protest arrest count to 1,800
